g.text: C370 · Why photonic circuits need compact models

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: Book Sec. 9.1 · what works for one component does not scale well to a whole circuit — so each element gets a fast compact model

g.text: circuit simulation with compact models can include such layout effects

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 9px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: Takeaway: physics solvers per component → optoelectronic parameters → compact models → fast, layout-aware simulation of the whole circuit.

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: Book Sec. 9.1 (p. 313). All drawings are schematic illustrations, not simulations. CMOS-industry solutions are “beginning to be incorporated” into photonic design.
